name: Medicare Care Compare
description: Compare published Medicare provider and quality information.
next_step: Compare published Medicare provider and quality information.

name: Pension additions: Aid and Attendance or Housebound
description: Extra monthly payments added to VA pension for qualifying veterans or survivors who need daily help or are housebound.
next_step: Ask an accredited representative about pension eligibility and Aid and Attendance. For a nursing home resident, ask about VA Form 21-0779; medical evidence is also required.

name: Dependency and Indemnity Compensation
description: A potential survivor benefit when a service member died in the line of duty or a veteran’s death meets VA’s service-related or other qualifying rules.
next_step: Ask an accredited representative whether DIC should be explored and what evidence is needed.

name: Increased VA disability compensation
description: A review route for an existing service-connected disability that has worsened.
next_step: Ask an accredited representative what evidence may support a request for an increased rating.

name: VA Program of Comprehensive Assistance for Family Caregivers
description: A VA caregiver assistance program with specific veteran and caregiver eligibility requirements.
next_step: Ask the VA caregiver support team about eligibility and the application process.

name: VA Program of General Caregiver Support Services
description: VA resources and support for people caring for veterans.
next_step: Ask the veteran’s VA care team which caregiver supports fit the situation.

name: VA hospice care
description: VA hospice care focuses on comfort and support near the end of life.
next_step: Ask the treating clinician or VA social worker about hospice assessment and coordination.

name: VA palliative care
description: Palliative care addresses symptoms, comfort and care goals for serious illness.
next_step: Ask the treating clinician about palliative care options.

name: VA pension during Medicaid-covered nursing home care
description: VA pension payments can be affected by Medicaid-covered nursing home care. The rules depend on the beneficiary’s circumstances.
next_step: Ask an accredited representative and the care facility’s benefits staff to review VA pension and Medicaid together before changing benefits.

name: Survivors Pension
description: A potential monthly benefit for qualifying surviving spouses and dependent children of wartime veterans, subject to income, net worth and other requirements.
next_step: Ask an accredited representative to screen for Survivors Pension and explain the evidence needed.

name: VA burial allowance and memorial routes
description: Ask the county office or VA burial program about the correct application.
next_step: Ask the county office or VA burial program about the correct application.

name: VA Community Living Centers
description: VA-operated Community Living Centers provide nursing home level care for eligible veterans.
next_step: Ask the VA care team or social worker about eligibility, assessment and local availability.

name: VA Community Nursing Home program
description: A VA pathway for care in participating community nursing homes, subject to eligibility and available services.
next_step: Ask the resident’s VA care team or social worker about community nursing home options.

name: VA health care enrollment
description: Apply for VA health care or get help understanding the enrollment process.
next_step: Call VA enrollment or ask your county veterans office about the application and supporting information.

name: Veterans Pension
description: Monthly pension for qualifying wartime veterans who meet age or disability, income, net worth and service requirements.
next_step: Ask an accredited representative to screen for pension and explain how care expenses may affect the application.

name: We Honor Veterans public resources
description: Use public veteran-care resources and ask the clinical team about coordinated care.
next_step: Use public veteran-care resources and ask the clinical team about coordinated care.
organization: National Alliance for Care at Home

name: VA Home Improvements and Structural Alterations (HISA)
description: Medically necessary changes to a veteran’s primary home, including permanent ramps, accessible bathrooms and widened access. Some non-service-connected needs can qualify.
next_step: Ask your VA care team for a clinical review and contact your VA medical facility’s Prosthetic and Sensory Aids Service. Confirm your remaining lifetime benefit and obtain the HISA application checklist.
constraints: HISA excludes portable ramps, stair glides, new construction and routine home repairs. VA determines eligibility, medical necessity and the available benefit. Prepare VA Form 10-0103, a VA-written or approved prescription, owner authorization (notarized for renters), an itemized estimate and a before photograph.

name: VA Specially Adapted Housing (SAH) grant
description: A housing grant route for veterans with qualifying service-connected disabilities.
next_step: Review the qualifying disability and ownership rules with VA or an accredited representative. Apply online through VA or use VA Form 26-4555; ask VA about project planning and approval before construction.
constraints: These grants require specific qualifying service-connected disabilities; a disability rating alone does not establish eligibility. Confirm the current fiscal-year maximum and any benefit already used with VA.

name: VA Special Housing Adaptation (SHA) grant
description: A housing adaptation grant route with specific service-connected disability requirements.
next_step: Review the qualifying disability and ownership rules with VA or an accredited representative. Apply online through VA or use VA Form 26-4555; ask VA about project planning and approval before construction.
constraints: These grants require specific qualifying service-connected disabilities; a disability rating alone does not establish eligibility. Confirm the current fiscal-year maximum and any benefit already used with VA.

name: Get a missing DD214 or service record
description: Request military records that may help document service for a benefits application.
next_step: Use the National Archives request instructions or ask the county veterans office for help. Who may request records and any fee depend on the record and request.

name: Find accredited help with a VA claim
description: Find and appoint an accredited representative for a benefits claim or decision review. Accredited VSO claims assistance is free.
next_step: Use VA’s representative search, then ask the representative if they are available. Attorneys and claims agents may charge fees.

name: Find a VA medical facility or benefits office
description: Search for VA locations near the resident and identify where to ask about care or benefits.
next_step: Use the official locator with the resident’s city or ZIP code and select the kind of facility needed.

name: Veteran housing and homelessness help
description: A 24-hour VA contact for veterans who are homeless or at risk of losing housing.
next_step: Call 877-424-3838, available 24/7, if homeless or at risk of losing housing. Family, care teams and supporters may also call. Ask for local VA and community housing support.

name: VA Temporary Residence Adaptation (TRA)
description: Changes to a family member’s home where a qualifying veteran or service member is living temporarily.
next_step: Ask VA about TRA if you qualify for SAH or SHA and are temporarily living in a family member’s home.
constraints: TRA requires SAH or SHA eligibility; it is not a general temporary-housing or renter grant.

name: Memory loss and dementia: 24/7 support
description: Free, confidential dementia information, caregiver support and referrals to local community resources.
next_step: Call the Alzheimer’s Association helpline for care planning, local support groups and caregiver guidance. Seek medical evaluation for new memory concerns.
constraints: The helpline provides support and referrals; it does not replace clinical assessment or emergency services.

name: American Legion: find a local post
description: Official post lookup for community connections and identifying public contacts to share the guide with.
next_step: Search the official directory for your town or ZIP code. Confirm the post’s public phone or email and ask who handles community partnerships.
constraints: A local post is not automatically an accredited claims office or a funding provider. Confirm its services, membership or visitor rules, accessibility and current contact details.

name: AMVETS: find a local post
description: Official post lookup for community connections and identifying public contacts to share the guide with.
next_step: Search the official directory for your town or ZIP code. Confirm the post’s public phone or email and ask who handles community partnerships.
constraints: A local post is not automatically an accredited claims office or a funding provider. Confirm its services, membership or visitor rules, accessibility and current contact details.

name: VFW: find a local post
description: Official post lookup for community connections and identifying public contacts to share the guide with.
next_step: Search the official directory for your town or ZIP code. Confirm the post’s public phone or email and ask who handles community partnerships.
constraints: A local post is not automatically an accredited claims office or a funding provider. Confirm its services, membership or visitor rules, accessibility and current contact details.

name: Suicide and emotional crisis support: 988
description: Crisis counseling and referrals for people in suicidal crisis or emotional distress, including veterans and concerned supporters.
next_step: Call or text 988 for crisis support. Veterans-specific support is available through the call service. For immediate danger, call 911 or go to the nearest emergency department.
constraints: Crisis support is separate from benefits eligibility and scheduled mental health treatment.

name: Veterans: mental health care and suicide prevention
description: VA mental health care, suicide-prevention guidance, counseling and routes to VA medical centers and Vet Centers. Some services are available without VA enrollment.
next_step: Use the VA page to connect with care. Existing patients can ask their primary care provider; others can contact a VA medical center or Vet Center. For urgent emotional distress, use 988 instead of waiting for an appointment.
constraints: Confirm which services fit the person’s eligibility and needs. Scheduled care is not a substitute for immediate crisis help.

name: Housing stability: Supportive Services for Veteran Families (SSVF)
description: Housing stability services through community organizations for low-income veteran families experiencing homelessness or imminent housing loss.
next_step: Use the SSVF Providers link on the VA page to find an awarded organization. Ask about county coverage, prevention or rapid rehousing, eligibility and current assistance.
constraints: Provider service areas, funding and eligibility vary. An award or referral does not guarantee financial assistance.

name: HUD-VASH: housing vouchers and VA support
description: Housing voucher assistance paired with VA case management for veterans experiencing homelessness who need ongoing support.
next_step: Call VA homelessness routing at 877-424-3838 and ask whether HUD-VASH screening is appropriate. Ask about local assessment, vouchers and housing availability.
constraints: Screening, program criteria, voucher availability and qualifying housing requirements apply; immediate housing is not guaranteed.
organization: U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs / HUD

name: VA Community Resource and Referral Centers
description: Find walk-in community resource centers connecting homeless and at-risk veterans with VA and non-VA services.
next_step: Use the official center directory and confirm the nearest location, hours and intake. If no nearby center is listed, call VA homelessness routing at 877-424-3838.
constraints: Centers are not present in every county. Confirm local access and resources; a listing does not guarantee a shelter bed.

name: VA disability compensation
description: Compensation for veterans with an illness or injury connected to their military service, including conditions VA presumes are service-connected.
next_step: A county veterans office or another accredited representative can help you file. You can also file online, by mail or in person. For questions, call the VA benefits hotline, Monday through Friday, 8 a.m. to 9 p.m. ET.
constraints: VA decides eligibility and ratings. This guide does not prepare or file claims.

name: Disagree with a VA decision: Supplemental Claims
description: A way to ask VA to look again at a decided claim when you have new and relevant evidence, or when the law has changed.
next_step: Ask an accredited representative whether this review fits your decision. A Supplemental Claim can be filed online for disability compensation, or by mail or in person for other benefits.
constraints: This is one of VA's decision review options. An accredited representative can explain the choices.

name: Toxic exposure and the PACT Act
description: The PACT Act expands VA health care and benefits for veterans exposed to burn pits, Agent Orange and other toxic substances, including veterans of the Vietnam, Gulf War and post-9/11 eras.
next_step: Ask for a toxic exposure screening at your next VA health care appointment, or contact your local VA health facility and ask for the toxic exposure screening navigator. For questions, call VA at 800-698-2411.
constraints: The screening is for veterans enrolled in VA health care. VA decides eligibility for care and benefits.

name: Women Veterans Call Center
description: A free, confidential VA line that helps women veterans find VA services and resources. A friend, relative or caregiver may call for her.
next_step: Call or text 855-829-6636, Monday through Friday, 8 a.m. to 10 p.m. ET, and Saturday, 8 a.m. to 6:30 p.m. ET, or use the online chat on the VA page.
constraints: Closed on federal holidays. In a crisis, call 988 and press 1.

name: Vet Centers: counseling in your community
description: Community counseling centers that offer individual, group, marriage and family counseling at no cost to eligible veterans, service members (including National Guard and Reserve) and their families.
next_step: Call the Vet Center Call Center at 877-927-8387, at any hour, to talk with someone or to be connected with the nearest Vet Center.
constraints: Eligibility depends on the kind of service or experience, such as service in a combat theater or military sexual trauma. Ask the Vet Center.

name: Counseling after military sexual trauma
description: Counseling at Vet Centers for any veteran or service member, including National Guard and Reserve members, who experienced military sexual trauma, whenever they served.
next_step: Call the Vet Center Call Center at 877-927-8387 and ask about military sexual trauma counseling. In a crisis, call 988 and press 1.

name: GI Bill and VA education benefits
description: Help paying for college, job training and career counseling for veterans, service members and qualified family members.
next_step: Check eligibility and apply on VA's education page, or call the GI Bill hotline, Monday through Friday, 7 a.m. to 6 p.m. Central. A school's VA certifying official can also help you apply.
constraints: Benefits depend on your service and the program you choose. VA decides eligibility.

name: Veteran Readiness and Employment (Chapter 31)
description: Job training, help finding or returning to work, self-employment support and independent living services for veterans and service members whose service-connected disability limits their ability to work.
next_step: Apply online, by mail or at a VA regional office. If you are eligible, VA invites you to an orientation session.
constraints: For veterans, VA's eligibility page asks for a service-connected disability rating of at least 10% and a discharge that is not dishonorable.

name: Job help at American Job Centers
description: Employment and training services through a national network of more than 2,400 American Job Centers. Veterans and eligible spouses receive priority of service in U.S. Department of Labor job training programs.
next_step: Find the nearest American Job Center at careeronestop.org or call 877-872-5627. Tell the staff you are a veteran or an eligible spouse so priority of service applies.

name: VA home loans
description: VA-backed home loans for veterans, service members and eligible surviving spouses.
next_step: Start by getting a Certificate of Eligibility, online or through your lender. To speak with a VA loan technician, call 877-827-3702.

name: Veteran ID cards
description: Ways to show veteran status: the digital Veteran ID Card, the Veteran Health Identification Card used at VA appointments, a Department of Defense ID, or a veteran designation on a state driver's license or ID.
next_step: Choose the card that fits you on VA's page and apply online. Have your discharge papers ready for the Veteran ID Card.
constraints: The Veteran ID Card is for veterans with an honorable or general discharge. The health ID card requires enrollment in VA health care.

name: Discharge upgrade or correction
description: Step-by-step instructions for asking a military board to upgrade or correct a discharge. If the discharge is upgraded, the veteran becomes eligible for the VA benefits earned during that period of service.
next_step: Answer the questions on VA's page to get the forms and the mailing address for your situation, or ask a veterans service organization to help. For questions, call 800-827-1000, Monday through Friday, 8 a.m. to 9 p.m. ET.
constraints: You apply by mail or with the help of a veterans service organization.

name: VA Solid Start: your first year out
description: VA representatives contact newly separated service members three times during the first year after active duty to explain benefits such as health care, housing assistance and education.
next_step: Keep your contact information with VA up to date and take the call. To reach Solid Start, call 800-827-0611, Monday through Friday, 8 a.m. to 9 p.m. ET.

name: Idaho veterans: Office of Veterans Advocacy for claims help
organization: Idaho Division of Veterans Services, Office of Veterans Advocacy
description: Free help with VA claims, appeals, pension and survivor benefits from the Idaho Division of Veterans Services’ accredited state service officers, in offices in Boise, Caldwell, Mountain Home, Twin Falls, Pocatello, Lewiston and Post Falls.
next_step: Call the office nearest you, or the Central Support Office at 208-780-1300, to make an appointment with a veterans service officer.
constraints: Offices are open Monday to Friday, 8 a.m. to 4:30 p.m.; messages can be left 24 hours a day.
Most counties have no state office; many have a county veterans service officer at the courthouse.

description: Idaho’s six Area Agencies on Aging, coordinated by the Idaho Commission on Aging, are the local starting point for older adults, people with disabilities and caregivers: information and assistance, meals, help at home, caregiver support, legal assistance and adult protection. Military service is not required.
next_step: Choose a county above for its Area Agency on Aging, call the Idaho Commission on Aging at 877-471-2777, or dial 2-1-1.
constraints: Each program has its own eligibility and waitlist.

name: Medicare counseling (SHIBA) for Idaho
organization: Idaho Department of Insurance, Senior Health Insurance Benefits Advisors (SHIBA)
description: Free, unbiased Medicare counseling from Idaho’s State Health Insurance Assistance Program, SHIBA: plan choices, enrollment, costs and help with Medicare complaints, in person, by phone or by email.
next_step: Call the SHIBA Medicare Help Line at 800-247-4422 or use the Ask SHIBA form. For Medicare itself, call 800-MEDICARE (800-633-4227).
constraints: SHIBA does not sell insurance or recommend specific plans. Have your Medicare card and drug list ready.

name: Idaho Long-Term Care Ombudsman and adult abuse reporting
organization: Idaho Commission on Aging, Long-Term Care Ombudsman Program
description: Advocacy for residents of skilled nursing and assisted living facilities. Idaho’s local ombudsmen and Adult Protective Services both work through the six Area Agencies on Aging.
next_step: Call the Area Agency on Aging for the county (choose a county above) and ask for the long-term care ombudsman, or call the State Ombudsman at the Idaho Commission on Aging, 877-471-2777. To report abuse, neglect or exploitation of a vulnerable adult, call the same Area Agency on Aging. In an emergency, call 911.
constraints: The ombudsman acts with the resident’s permission and is not a licensing agency.

name: Free legal help for Idaho older adults
description: Idaho Legal Aid Services gives free civil legal help to Idahoans 60 and older and to people with low incomes, including a Senior and Public Benefits Legal Advice Line. The Area Agencies on Aging also arrange legal assistance for older adults.
next_step: Call 208-746-7541 for the Legal Advice Lines (phone intake Monday to Wednesday, 10 a.m. to 1:30 p.m. Mountain Time), or apply online. For questions about a lawyer, the Idaho State Bar is at 208-334-4500.
constraints: Legal aid screens by age, income, assets and case type. It does not handle criminal cases.

name: VA health care systems serving Idaho
description: Idaho veterans are served by four VA health care systems: VA Boise (Boise VA Medical Center, 500 West Fort Street; 208-422-1000 or toll-free 866-437-5093); VA Spokane, which serves northern Idaho; VA Walla Walla, whose Lewiston VA Clinic is at 1630 23rd Avenue, Building 2; and VA Salt Lake City, whose clinics include Pocatello.
next_step: Use VA’s facility locator with your ZIP code to find the closest clinic. Not enrolled yet? Ask an Office of Veterans Advocacy service officer for help applying.
constraints: Which system serves you depends on where you live; VA’s locator shows the right clinic.

description: A Center for Independent Living: disability-led help with daily living skills, peer support, advocacy, assistive technology referrals and moving from a nursing home back to the community. Any age and any disability; military service is not required.
next_step: Call with your county and goals. Ask about intake, home access, independent living skills or help leaving a facility.
constraints: A Center for Independent Living is a community support organization, not a residential care facility. Services depend on assessment and availability.

name: LIFE, A Center for Independent Living (Burley)
organization: LIFE, A Center for Independent Living
description: A Center for Independent Living: disability-led help with daily living skills, peer support, advocacy, assistive technology referrals and moving from a nursing home back to the community. Any age and any disability; military service is not required.
next_step: Call with your county and goals. Ask about intake, home access, independent living skills or help leaving a facility.
constraints: A Center for Independent Living is a community support organization, not a residential care facility. Services depend on assessment and availability.
Office: 2311 Park Avenue, Suite 7, Burley, ID 83318. Voice/TTY: 208-678-7705.

name: El-Ada, Inc.: veteran housing help (SSVF)
description: VA-funded Supportive Services for Veteran Families (SSVF, grant 12-ID-032): case management, help keeping a home, rapid rehousing and short-term financial help for low-income veteran households.
next_step: Call SSVF intake with your county and housing situation: whether you are homeless now or at risk of losing housing, and who lives with you. A second intake number is listed: 208-854-9878.
constraints: Serves only the areas listed; check that yours is included. Veteran-household, income and housing-status screening applies.
County and intake details come from VA’s FY26 SSVF provider intake list; confirm current service when calling.

name: North Idaho Area Agency on Aging (Area 1)
organization: North Idaho Area Agency on Aging (Area 1)
description: The Area Agency on Aging for this county: information and assistance, home-delivered and congregate meals, in-home services, transportation, caregiver support and senior legal assistance.
next_step: Call and describe what is hard right now. Ask for information and assistance. You can also call the Idaho Commission on Aging at 877-471-2777 or dial 2-1-1. Military service is not required.
constraints: Many services focus on people age 60 and older and adults with disabilities; eligibility and waitlists vary by program.

organization: Long-Term Care Ombudsman, North Idaho Area Agency on Aging (Area 1)
description: The regional long-term care ombudsman for this county: advocacy for residents of nursing homes, assisted living and residential care facilities.
next_step: Call the regional ombudsman program. Give the facility name and county. For immediate danger, call 911.
constraints: The ombudsman acts with the resident’s permission and is not a licensing or enforcement agency.
